title: Nuanced Tense and Aspect
summary: Refine how Portuguese presents actions as completed, ongoing, habitual, repeated, or consequential.

sections.heading: Preterite vs imperfect as viewpoint
sections.body: At advanced levels, the difference is not just 'completed' vs 'ongoing'; it is the speaker's viewpoint. The preterite frames an event as bounded. The imperfect opens a scene or presents a habit/state without clear boundaries.

examples.pt: Ele entrou, sentou e pediu café.
examples.en: He came in, sat down, and ordered coffee.

examples.pt: Ele entrava, sentava e pedia café todos os dias.
examples.en: He used to come in, sit down, and order coffee every day.
I wanted to talk to you.

sections.heading: Ter + participle vs simple preterite
sections.body: **Tenho feito** emphasizes repetition or continuity into the present. The simple preterite states that an event happened. Choosing one changes the aspect, not just the tense.

examples.pt: Tenho lido muito sobre o assunto.
examples.en: I have been reading a lot about the subject.

examples.pt: A empresa tem investido em tecnologia.
examples.en: The company has been investing in technology.

sections.heading: Ir + infinitive and future forms
sections.body: Brazilian speech favors **ir + infinitive** for future actions, while the simple future sounds more formal, predictive, or emphatic. The future can also express probability.

examples.en: I will send the file today.
I will send the file today.
He is probably at home now.

keyPoints: Aspect is about how an action is viewed, not only when it happens.
Preterite bounds events; imperfect opens scenes or habits.
Tenho feito implies repeated/ongoing relevance to now.
Simple future is formal and can express probability.

commonMistakes.note: Specific finished past event uses preterite.

commonMistakes.wrong: Quando era criança, fui ao clube todo sábado.
commonMistakes.right: Quando era criança, ia ao clube todo sábado.

commonMistakes.wrong: Ele vai estar em casa agora.
commonMistakes.right: Ele deve estar em casa agora. / Ele estará em casa agora.
commonMistakes.note: For probability, use deve estar or formal future.
